name: Ecosystems and Human Impact, BA
degree: Bachelor of Arts in Ecosystems and Human Impact

requirements.label: Foundation
requirements.title: Required Foundation Courses for Major (27-28 credits)

rules.manualCheck: If students do not place into MAT 125, MAT 131, or AMS 151 on the basis of the math placement examination, MAT 123 (or MAT 119/MAT 123) is a required course for the major.

requirements.sourceText: ANT 120 - Introduction to Biological Anthropology 3 credits; BIO 201 - Fundamentals of Biology: Organisms to Ecosystems 3 credits; BIO 204 - Fundamentals of Scientific Inquiry in the Biological Sciences I 2 credits; CHE 115 - Chemistry, Life, and Environment 3 credits; ENV 115 - Chemistry, Life, and Environment 3 credits (Note: CHE 129, CHE 131, or CHE 152 may be substituted for CHE 115/ENV 115); ECO 108 - Introduction to Economics 4 credits; MAT 125 - Calculus A 3 credits OR MAT 130 - Trigonometry and Logarithms 1 credit, MAT 125 - Calculus A Credits: 3 credits OR MAT 131 - Calculus I 4 credits OR AMS 151 - Applied Calculus I 3 credits If students do not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131 or AMS 151 on the basis of the math placement examination, MAT 123 (or MAT 119/MAT 123) is a required course for the major.; SUS 111 - Introduction to Sustainability 3 credits OR ENS 101 - Prospects for Planet Earth 3 credits; SUS 201 - Systems and Models 3 credits; SUS 204 - Population Studies 3 credits

requirements.label: Core
requirements.title: Core Courses (24-25 credits)
requirements.sourceText: BIO 351 - Ecology 3 credits; ENV 301 - Sustainability of the Long Island Pine Barrens 3 credits OR SUS 401 - Integrative, Collaborative Systems Studies 3 credits; ENV 304 - Global Environmental Change 3 credits OR ATM 305 - Global Atmospheric Change 3 credits; GSS 313 - GIS Design and Application I 3 credits; GSS 314 - GIS Laboratory 1 credit OR GIS 317 - Geospatial Narratives; SUS 301 - Technical Writing and Communication 3 credits; SUS 305 - Collective Action and Advocacy 3 credits; SUS 322 - Human Ecology 3 credits; SUS 326 - Conservation Genetics 3 credits

requirements.title: Elective Group I: Technical Skills

rule.manualCheck: SUS 488, SUS 487, ANP 387, ANP 487, and ANT 487 may be taken as a three-credit course only with permission of the faculty advisor. Other classes may be substituted with permission of the undergraduate director.

requirements.label: Writing
requirements.title: Communications and Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: Requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and approval of a term paper or laboratory report written for an advanced course in the major (including Readings and Research courses). Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S approves the WRTD requirement. Preapproved courses are available from the department.

requirements.sourceText: The advanced writing component of the major in EHI requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and approval of either a term paper or a laboratory report written for an advanced course in the appropriate major at Stony Brook (including Readings and Research courses). Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S will result in approval of the WRTD requirement.

requirements.label: Grade exception
requirements.title: Grade below C limit

rule.text: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major.
rule.reason: Limits the number and credits of sub-C courses across the whole major, which no rule type covers.

requirements.sourceText: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major. Course taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.

requirements.label: Double majors
requirements.title: Double major 300-400 level credit limit

rule.text: Excluding ENV 301, SUS 301, SUS 305, and SUS 401, no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the Sustainability Studies Program or the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.
rule.reason: Program-wide credit limit across two majors, which no rule type covers.

requirements.sourceText: Excluding ENV 301 - Sustainability of the Long Island Pine Barrens, SUS 301 - Technical Writing and Communication, SUS 305 - Collective Action and Advocacy, and SUS 401 - Integrative, Collaborative Systems Studies, no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the Sustainability Studies Program or the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.

policies.sourceText: Course taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.

substitutions.sourceText: AMS 110, AMS 310, ECO 320 or POL 201 may be substituted for BIO 211
Note: CHE 129, CHE 131, or CHE 152 may be substituted for CHE 115/ENV 115

fulfillment.sourceText: Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S will result in approval of the WRTD requirement.

notes.text: Effective Spring 2023, students may not declare the major in Ecosystems and Human Impact. Students may instead enroll in the Ecosystems and Human Impact track in the BA in Sustainability Studies.

Students should consult with the department advisor to ensure that their plan for completing the Upper Division Writing Requirement is consistent with university graduation requirements for General Education. Students are encouraged to talk with the major director about how study abroad coursework can be used to fulfill major requirements.

Study abroad is available in Cuba, Madagascar, and the Turkana Basin (Kenya). Students may enroll in the study abroad program at Ranomafana, Madagascar in their junior or senior year. Local internships, research courses, and field courses are also available.
Students completing the Stony Brook Curriculum must complete a course that satisfies the WRTD learning objective to graduate.
